userPrompt: Does the GDPR let me keep customer data forever if I got consent once?
responseText:
**No.**

GDPR does **not** let you keep customer data forever just because you obtained consent once.

### Key rules
- **Consent must be informed, specific, and freely given** (Art. 6(1)(a), Art. 7, Recital 32). A vague “we may use your data for anything” consent is invalid.
- **Consent can be withdrawn at any time** (Art. 7(3)). When the customer withdraws, you must stop processing and, in most cases, delete the data unless another lawful basis applies.
- **Storage limitation principle** (Art. 5(1)(e)): You may keep personal data only as long as it is necessary for the purposes for which it was collected. “Forever” almost never satisfies this.

Even with valid initial consent, you must:
- Define clear retention periods (e.g., “we will delete your data 2 years after your last order or after you withdraw consent, whichever comes first”).
- Periodically review whether the original purpose still exists.
- Delete or anonymize the data once the purpose is fulfilled or consent is withdrawn.

### Practical answer
One-time consent does **not** give you a perpetual license to store customer data indefinitely. You must delete it when it is no longer necessary or when the data subject objects/withdraws consent and no other lawful basis (contract, legal obligation, legitimate interest) justifies continued storage.

If you want to keep data longer, you usually need a different lawful basis or must demonstrate a continuing legitimate purpose that outweighs the individual’s rights. Most companies set fixed retention schedules and delete after a defined period (e.g., 3–7 years depending on the relationship and legal requirements).
